settings.heading: Three generations behind one counter
settings.lede: Singhania Fabrics sells cloth the way the market has always sold it — off the than, cut to your metre, at the rate the trade pays. The site is only the counter, moved somewhere you can reach it at eleven at night.

settings.heading: How the rate works
settings.body: One rate, printed. Cross the slab — usually ten or eleven metres — and the lower rate applies to the whole cut, not just the metres past it. Nothing is marked up to be discounted back down.

settings.heading: Why every shade has a name
settings.body: Screen colour cannot be trusted, and the dye lot moves. Each shade carries the name the godown uses, so a phone call about "Indigo on 60x60" reaches the same bolt every time. Order the swatch card before a large cut.

settings.heading: Cutting and dispatch
settings.body: Cut in half-metre steps, folded, and dispatched the same evening for orders placed before 5 pm. Cut cloth cannot be taken back, which is the one rule the counter has never bent.

settings.heading: Visit the shop
settings.body: 2nd floor, Mangaldas Market, Kalbadevi Road. Monday to Saturday, 10.30 am to 7.30 pm. Ask for the design book at the counter — it holds more than the site.
